title: The Battle of Tours
description: October 732. Charles Martel's Frankish infantry must hold the wooded high ground between Tours and Poitiers against the Umayyad cavalry of Abd al-Rahman. A third force of Aquitanian allies under Duke Odo can be rallied to strike the enemy camp. Victory requires repelling the cavalry charges and forcing the invaders' withdrawal.

anachronisms_found: WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR standing in for Charles Martel: a Norman duke of 1066, over three centuries too late, and visually a mounted Norman knight rather than a Frankish infantry commander holding a shield wall
SALADIN standing in for Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi: an Ayyubid Kurdish sultan of the 1180s Levant, 450 years and 3,000 km removed from the Umayyad governor of al-Andalus
EL_CID standing in for Duke Odo of Aquitaine: an 11th-century Castilian, and ironically a Christian Iberian hero of the Reconquista, not a Merovingian-era Aquitanian duke
CAMEL_RIDER x4 in the Umayyad force: the Andalusi army that crossed the Pyrenees was Arab-Berber horse cavalry; camels were not campaign mounts in Gaul
CROSSBOWMAN x2 for the Franks: the crossbow was not a Frankish field weapon in 732; ARCHER/SKIRMISHER alone would have been safer
PIKEMAN x4 and CHAMPION x3: pike formations and plate-armoured champions are late-medieval; the engine's SPEARMAN/MILITIA line was available and closer to a 8th-century Frankish shield wall
KNIGHT x9 for the Umayyads and KNIGHT x6 for Aquitaine: barded, lance-armed Western European heavy horse of the 12th-13th centuries rather than lighter Andalusi or Aquitanian cavalry
MONASTERY and MARKET-with-GUARD_TOWER complexes are High Medieval structures for a 732 battlefield encampment
Text announces cavalry surging 'across the ford' but no water or shallows appear anywhere in the placed terrain

issues_found: Charles Martel is represented by WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR — a Norman duke of 1066, three centuries later and a different polity; a renamed generic Champion or Teutonic-style infantry hero would have been the correct substitution.
Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi is represented by SALADIN — a 12th-century Ayyubid Kurd, wrong dynasty, wrong culture and 450 years out of period. The victory trigger literally fires on 'SALADIN'.
Duke Odo of Aquitaine is represented by EL_CID — an 11th-century Castilian, wrong century and wrong realm; Odo was a Frankish/Aquitanian duke.
Both active players are set to civilization RANDOM, so architecture and unit skins are unassigned; Franks and (for the Umayyads) Saracens were both available and would have been trivially correct.
Player 3 (the Aquitanians) is not assigned a civilization at all in the listing.

Umayyad force includes CAMEL_RIDER x4 and Frankish force includes CROSSBOWMAN x2 and an ARCHERY_RANGE — crossbows are anachronistic for 732 and the Andalusian army was primarily horse, not camelry; Knights/Scout Cavalry alone would have been closer.
The Frankish 'camp' anchored on a TOWN_CENTER with Market, Monastery and Guard Towers implies a fortified settlement the Franks did not have on the Tours–Poitiers road.

Charles Martel is represented by the WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR hero — a Norman duke of 1066, over three centuries after Tours; a renamed generic Champion or Teutonic-style infantry hero was available and would have been correct.
Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi is represented by SALADIN — a late-12th-century Kurdish Ayyubid sultan, wrong dynasty, wrong region and wrong era for an 8th-century Umayyad wali of al-Andalus.
Duke Odo of Aquitaine is represented by EL_CID — an 11th-century Castilian, again the wrong person and century.
Both active players are set to RANDOM civilization, so Frankish and Andalusian architecture and unit sets are left to chance rather than assigned (Franks and Saracens/Berbers were both available).
Player 2's Umayyad force fields CAMEL_RIDER units; the Andalusian army at Tours was overwhelmingly horse cavalry, and the engine's Knight/Light Cavalry mix already covered it.
The 'hidden Aquitanians under Odo who must be rallied by a messenger' is an invention — Odo's forces were already operating with Charles, not concealed off-map awaiting a signal.
Force scale is very thin (17 Frankish and 16 Umayyad combatants) for an engagement described as repeated mass cavalry charges against a shield wall.
The 'ford' the cavalry crosses in the narration is not represented by any terrain or water feature in the placed objects.
